business_problem: Canadian Tire had abundant customer data across many banners and business units, but over-centralized processes, duplicated data paths, uneven governance and limited advanced analytics access kept leaders from using that information quickly enough to drive personalization, reporting and business growth.
solution_summary: EY helped Canadian Tire redesign how customer data is governed, accessed and used so advanced analytics and AI could move closer to business teams. The work started with a data maturity assessment covering governance, accessibility, Power BI proficiency and advanced analytics and artificial intelligence capabilities. EY then mapped nearly 500 data paths and 165 processes, using that inventory to recommend a decentralized data-mesh model on the Microsoft Azure stack with a federated governance approach. The resulting architecture gives domain owners more local control while preserving shared standards, and it is supported by an expanded internal data and analytics organization staffed with new data scientists and managers. Power BI dashboards running on top of the new model help banners analyze product performance by SKU, while Canadian Tire's Triangle Rewards program uses richer real-time customer insights to target offers and future marketing opportunities more precisely.

solution_components.name: data mesh construct
solution_components.role: Distributes data ownership to business domains while preserving common standards and governance.

solution_components.name: Microsoft Power BI
solution_components.role: Presents dashboard insights that business units use for agile product and customer analysis.

solution_components.name: Triangle Rewards Program

data_flow: Customer data from many banners and business units is inventoried, realigned into the Azure-based data mesh and governed through a federated model. Business domains then consume the unified data through Power BI dashboards and programs such as Triangle Rewards to analyze product performance, buyer patterns and marketing opportunities.
business_outcome: Canadian Tire created a more agile customer-data foundation that improves data access, strengthens personalization and enables business teams to use analytics faster, supporting better merchandising, loyalty and customer-growth decisions across the enterprise.
architecture_clues: EY recommended a decentralized data mesh on the Microsoft Azure stack rather than a centralized data platform.
The governance model gives domain owners localized autonomy with shared standards.
Power BI is the business-facing analytics layer for new dashboards.
Canadian Tire created a new internal data and analytics organization to run the operating model.
